am26.title: Third generation of the successful SUV: new Audi Q7 combines versatility and performance

generations.name: First generation

codes.quote: The Q7 (internally designated Typ 4L) utilizes a modified version of the Volkswagen Group PL71 platform.

revealed.quote: unveiled in September 2005 at the Frankfurt Motor Show

productionStart.quote: Production of the Q7 began in November 2005 at the Volkswagen Bratislava Plant in Bratislava, Slovakia.

salesStart.quote: The Q7 was the first SUV sold by Audi and went on sale in 2006.
The production version went on sale in July 2006.

revealed.quote: The vehicle was unveiled at the 2009 Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance.

changes.text: New front and rear lights with more LED lighting, new wheel designs, chrome accents and revised front and rear styling.
changes.quote: Exterior changes include new front and rear lights which better incorporate LED lighting with optional LED turn signals and daytime running lights, new wheel designs, chrome accents, four new paint colours, and updated body styling in the front and rear.

changes.text: New instrument cluster, new trim and colours, and the third-generation MMI control system.
changes.quote: A redesigned interior includes a new instrument cluster, new leather seating, ambient door lighting, new interior colour choices, new trim, and the third generation MMI control system.

changes.text: The 4.2-litre diesel was revised, rising from 240 kW (326 PS) to 250 kW (340 PS).
changes.quote: Zudem wurde der 4,2 Liter große Diesel überarbeitet und leistete nun 250 kW (340 PS) statt 240 kW (326 PS).

changes.text: The eight-speed automatic became standard from 2010 (2011 model year in the US).
changes.quote: From 2010 (2011 model year in the U.S.), the Aisin–Toyota 8-speed automatic transmission is standard.

changes.text: For 2011, the 3.6 FSI and 4.2 FSI engines were replaced by two supercharged 3.0 TFSI engines.
changes.quote: For 2011, the 3.6 FSI and 4.2 FSI engines were replaced by two 3.0 L TFSI supercharged engines.

notes: English Wikipedia's infobox gives production from November 2005; Audi's 2024 retrospective says first-generation production ran from 2006 to 2015 ("From the start of production in 2006 to the end of production of the first generation in 2015"). The Wikipedia figure is used here.
German Wikipedia gives slightly different dimensions (length 5086–5089 mm, width 1983 mm) from English Wikipedia (5085 mm, 1984 mm).

Facelift timing: German Wikipedia dates the facelift to spring 2009 and English Wikipedia says it was unveiled at Pebble Beach in 2009, but English Wikipedia's section heading reads 'Facelift (2010–2015)'.
The English Wikipedia engine tables label the year column 'Model Year'; whether these are calendar or model years is not stated. Engine figures are not tied to a market by the source.
A 6-speed manual was offered only in Europe with the 3.6 FSI (English Wikipedia). The 5-, 6- and 7-seat configurations are described in words only, so no seating figures are shown.
No Audi press release from 2005–2015 is cited; Audi information on the first generation comes from its 2024 retrospective.

changes.text: Up to 325 kg lighter than its predecessor according to Audi's press information.
changes.quote: laut Presseinformation um bis zu 325 Kilogramm leichter als sein Vorgänger

changes.text: Slightly smaller than the first generation.
changes.quote: Der zweite Audi Q7 ist geringfügig kleiner

changes.text: Doors, wings, bonnet and tailgate are made of aluminium.
changes.quote: Türen, Kotflügel, Motorhaube und Heckklappe sind aus Aluminium gefertigt.

changes.text: All-wheel steering became available as an option for all versions, a first for Audi.
changes.quote: Für alle Varianten war erstmals bei Audi auf Wunsch eine Allradlenkung erhältlich

changes.text: Built on the Volkswagen Group MLB Evo platform.
changes.quote: Platform Volkswagen Group MLB Evo

changes.text: All versions use a ZF 8HP eight-speed automatic.
changes.quote: Regardless of engine, all Q7's come with a ZF 8HP 8-speed automatic transmission

changes.text: A diesel plug-in hybrid was added, sold in Europe but not in Canada.
changes.quote: followed shortly by diesel-powered plug-in hybrid variant, which is sold in Europe, but not in Canada

revealed.quote: Im Sommer 2019 wurde sowohl beim Q7 als auch beim SQ7 ein Facelift durchgeführt.

changes.text: Redesigned grille, front and rear bumpers, new side sills, chrome tailgate trim and revised exhaust tips.
changes.quote: introducing styling tweaks such as a redesigned grille, front and rear bumpers, new side sills, chrome trim for the tailgate and revised exhaust tips

changes.text: New infotainment system with two touchscreens; dashboard and centre console updated to suit.
changes.quote: Inside, Audi installed a new infotainment system with dual touchscreens. The dashboard and centre console were also updated to accommodate the new system.

changes.text: Three mild-hybrid 3.0-litre V6 engines: two diesels and one petrol.
changes.quote: Three mild-hybrid 3.0-litre V6 powertrains are available, with the choice of two diesels and one petrol.

changes.text: Active roll stabilisation added to the options list.
changes.quote: Audi has also expanded the Q7's options list to include a new active roll-stabilisation system

changes.text: New 55 TFSI e and 60 TFSI e plug-in hybrids were introduced for the European market at the end of 2019.
changes.quote: Ende 2019 wurden im Facelift mit dem 55 TFSI e quattro und 60 TFSI e quattro neue Plug-in-Hybrid-Varianten für den europäischen Markt vorgestellt.

revealed.quote: Audi announced a second facelift in January 2024 for the 2025 model year

changes.text: The Singleframe grille gained vertical inlays.
changes.quote: The unmistakably upright Audi Singleframe with an octagon design now impresses with vertical inlays.

changes.text: HD Matrix LED headlights with laser high beam gained selectable digital daytime running light signatures.
changes.quote: For the first time in a Q7, the HD Matrix LED headlights with laser as an additional high beam feature digital daytime running lights with selectable light signatures.

changes.text: Digital OLED rear lights with four selectable designs became available.
changes.quote: Digital OLED rear lights with four selectable rear light designs complete the light offering.

changes.text: The SQ7 TFSI uses the 4.0 TFSI V8 with 373 kW (507 PS) and 770 Nm.
changes.quote: the SQ7 TFSI now runs on the established 4.0 TFSI with 373 kW (507 PS) and 770 Nm of torque

changes.text: The plug-in hybrids received a battery of 25.9 kWh gross (22 kWh net).
changes.quote: The design achieves a maximum capacity of 25.9 kWh (gross; 22 kWh net) at 370 volts.

notes: Plug-in hybrid output conflict for the 3.0 TDI e-tron: German Wikipedia gives a system output of 275 kW (374 PS) and 700 Nm (recorded); English Wikipedia's table gives 387 PS (285 kW) / 700 Nm and its prose gives 190 kW / 600 Nm.

The 2.0 TFSI e-tron was developed for Asian markets (China, South Korea, Singapore and Japan) per English Wikipedia; the 2.0 TFSI was offered in Russia, the US, Canada, India, the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Because these sources name several markets at once, these powertrains are marked 'unstated'.
SQ7 TFSI displacement: English Wikipedia's table lists 3,956 cc (the diesel's figure); German Wikipedia gives 3,996 cm³. Audi's 2024 release says '4.0 TFSI' only, so no displacement is recorded.

Model years 2016–2026 are given by English Wikipedia without a market; North American model years are not documented separately. The first facelift was for the 2020 model year and the second for the 2025 model year (English Wikipedia).
UK sales of the first facelift started in September 2019 (English Wikipedia). US-market SQ7 used a 4.0 V8 petrol (500 hp / 770 Nm) from 2020 rather than the diesel (English Wikipedia).

Audi's 2024 release refers to 'an initial product upgrade in 2019' and 'a second comprehensive upgrade in 2023', although the release itself is dated 30 January 2024 and market launch was in the first quarter of 2024.

Audi's published dimension figures are not recorded here yet; the figures shown are from English Wikipedia without a stated version or market. German Wikipedia gives ranges (length 5052–5072 mm, wheelbase 2994–3001 mm).

generations.name: Third generation

revealed.quote: The third generation Q7 was revealed on 9 June 2026

salesStart.quote: It will be available to order in Germany from June 2026, with deliveries commencing in September.

platform.quote: It will be built on the Premium Platform Combustion platform.

assembly.quote: The new Q7 is built in Bratislava – just like the two previous generations.

drivetrains.quote: As standard, the Q7 is equipped with an eight-speed tiptronic and quattro permanent all-wheel drive with the new limited-slip center differential with preload.

cargo.quote: The five-seater has a trunk capacity of up to 806 liters.
Folding down the second-row seats expands the storage space to up to 2,075 liters.
The seven-seater offers up to 722 liters of luggage space behind the second row
a maximum volume of 1,980 liters behind the first row

changes.text: Moves to the Premium Platform Combustion.
changes.quote: It will be built on the Premium Platform Combustion platform.

changes.text: MHEV plus mild-hybrid technology, with a new powertrain generator, adds up to 18 kW (24 PS).
changes.quote: The MHEV plus technology, including a next-generation powertrain generator, supports the drivetrain with up to 18 kW (24 PS) of extra power.

changes.text: quattro all-wheel drive gains a new limited-slip centre differential with preload.
changes.quote: quattro permanent all-wheel drive with the new limited-slip center differential with preload

changes.text: A more upright D-pillar gives a nearly horizontal roofline and more interior headroom.
changes.quote: The D-pillar is now more upright overall, resulting in a nearly horizontal roofline and offering more headroom and space inside.

changes.text: Third-generation digital OLED rear lights with communication lighting.
changes.quote: At the rear, third-generation digital OLED rear lights feature communication lighting and an active digital light signature.

changes.text: Five seats are standard, with six- and seven-seat layouts optional.
changes.quote: The Q7 is available in three seating variants. Five seats come standard, with six or seven seats available as an option.

notes: Production start is not documented: English Wikipedia says 'Production 2026 (to commence)'. Audi's release gives ordering in Germany from June 2026 and deliveries from September (recorded as the EU sales start).
Dimensions come from English Wikipedia only (they look rounded: width 2,010 mm, height 1,800 mm); Audi's launch release gives no dimensions. Treat them as provisional.

Audi's launch release lists only the 3.0 V6 TDI (180 kW and 220 kW). The 2.9 V6 petrol and SQ7 V8 figures come from English Wikipedia, which cites US-oriented press (Motor1, Autoweek), and says Australia gets a 3.0 V6 diesel; their market is therefore marked 'unstated'.
Seating (5, 6 or 7 seats) is stated in words only, so it is listed among the changes rather than as seating figures.
